chapter_theme: The fullest statement in this run of Sivavakkiyar's oneness and his contempt for marks: the Lord who is everywhere entered our body, so 'your god and our god' is only your difference; caste is nothing to the knower; the body is ten months of the womb's impurity, so pride in it is madness. Against ash, guise, bathing and daily mantra he sets the yoga of the tongue turned back and the channel of sound, and the five letters pressed into the heart until the one letter behind them is known; the refrain Sivayam stands for that one.
structure_note: A running cut of one editorial heading (அறிவு நிலை). Runs within it: union and the five letters (1164 to 1167); the state beyond speech and the body from the womb's impurity (1168, 1169); the letters and the near-repeats of earlier stanzas (1170 to 1173); the name in the mouth, false rites and the womb again (1174 to 1177); book-learning and caste set against the knower (1178, 1179); yoga of tongue and channel, the fives, the letters, life and body, the ascent (1180 to 1185); and one god against two (1186 to 1188).

1164.reading: Only when our forms mingled did I know you; what matters it whether you stay or hide, when in every moment I thought of you we stood merged, so are you and I not one? Doubt mingled and went, and Sivayam became clear.
1164.nuance: The poet speaks to the Lord in the second person and claims identity (நீயும் நானும் ஒன்றலோ) as a question. திருக்கலந்து is ambiguous: 'the holy mingled' or 'doubt (திருக்கு, as the gloss on 1132 has it) mingled and left'; the second gives the better sense with தெளிந்தது (became clear).

1165.reading: Clarified in the five letters Sivayam one can become a god; clarified in them one can rule the sky; the thing of the sky is what is grasped with clarity in the five letters; and the truth is what is grasped with clarity in the five letters.
1165.nuance: சிவாயம் has four syllables but is called அஞ்செழுத்து, so the refrain stands for the five-letter mantra rather than spelling it. The first two lines promise godhood and rule of heaven, the last two the truth; the order ranks the powers below the knowing, and தெளிந்து (clarified) carries every line.

1166.reading: As a clay pot with the five hidden in it bobs on the water and spills its contents, so this body and its senses are tossed upon the waters; and as that pot, filling with water, sits settled, so this body, scooping up Siva, sits delighted and still.
1166.nuance: பொய்க்குடம், the false pot, is the body as fired clay; the five (ஐந்து) hidden in it are the elements or senses. The simile turns on what fills the pot: empty, it floats and spills; full, it sinks and rests. The body is not condemned, only shown as a vessel whose contents decide its motion.

1167.reading: The soul flies like a kite on its string; see it with the understanding that experience gives and tie the knot that will hold; do not let it be blamed, do not let the soul go; bind tight the thief who knows the theft.
1167.nuance: The string is the breath, in the tradition's reading, and the kite the soul or mind that would fly off. பட்டறிவு is knowledge from experience, set against book-knowledge. The thief who knows the theft (களவறிந்த கள்வன்) may be the mind, or the Lord himself, whom Tirumular calls the thief-chief who enters and leaves the body; binding him is then holding the Lord in the body.

1168.reading: Night gone, day gone, even the inner Brahman gone; beyond all the cosmic eggs, in form after countless form, the truth of the blissful nature where speech has died and mind has died: to speak it, there is no helper other than myself.
1168.nuance: அகப்பிரமம் இறந்து, the inner Brahman dying, places even the meditator's Brahman among the things that end. The last line (சொல்லியாற என்னில் வேறு துணைவர் இல்லை) is unclear: 'no one but I can tell it', or 'I have no companion but it'; ஆற may be ஆறு (the way) or a corrupt word.

1169.reading: What stayed gathered for ten months as the womb's impurity became two hands, two feet and two eyes, a body thick with sound, shining with taste and smell; and the 'pure' body it became is, when told truly, that impurity.
1169.nuance: The pairs (கை இரண்டு, கால் இரண்டு, கண் இரண்டு) and the sense-qualities (சத்தம், இரசம், கந்தம்) are the elements' marks, so the body is built from the tattvas out of the impurity. துய்ய காயம், the pure body, is said with irony; the stanza's last word is தூமை.

1170.reading: The pedestal of the linga in the body, the three letters of the unspoken mantra, the conch and the discus, all the sky; the yogis who have taken their share there, the five supreme gates and the lion-roar sound: nothing is other than Sivayam.
1170.nuance: The gloss gives அசவை as the ajapa mantra, the unrecited syllables of the breath (in tradition ஹம்ஸ or சோகம்), here counted as three letters. Conch and discus are Vishnu's, so the stanza claims the Vaishnava emblems for Sivayam too. பரம வாசல் அஞ்சு, the five supreme gates, is not fixed, perhaps the five senses or five centres. Near-repeat of 1138.

1171.reading: You devotees who keep saying 'the five letters and the three letters': the thing itself is neither the five letters nor the three. Press the five letters into the heart and know that letter, and the five letters take on the colour of that: Sivayam.
1171.nuance: The mantra is denied as the goal and kept as the means: the five pressed into the heart (நெஞ்சழுத்து) lead to 'that letter' (அவ்வெழுத்து), which is unnamed, and then the five become its colour. The three letters are அ உ ம, the parts of Om. The stanza is the poet's own gloss on his refrain: Sivayam is not the syllables.

1172.reading: When sleep comes to bewilder and forgets the cherished mantras, the Agamas composed, wife, children and kin, where did they go and hide, or did they stand become everywhere? Tell me, Lord, the place where they hid in the light.
1172.nuance: Near-repeat of 1114 with scripture in the place of secular books: the mantras one has cherished and the Agamas also vanish in sleep. 1114 asked the மாயம் (mystery) of their hiding; 1172 asks the இடம் (place), and மயக்க (bewilder) replaces மறக்க (forget).

1173.reading: Is the letter beginningless, is the soul beginningless? Are the elements and senses that have entered us beginningless? Are the worthy books beginningless, and is Sadasiva beginningless? Yogis who have come far, you must answer quickly.
1173.nuance: Near-repeat of 1126 with two changes: the true guru of 1126's last question becomes Sadasiva, so the Lord's own beginninglessness is put among the questions, and the yogis are told to answer at once (விரைந்து) where 1126 named no one to answer.

1174.reading: While the nine-gated body still has its days before it ceases, the name Rama, Rama, Rama, called the ninth: in the mouths of the spiteful it comes as a disease that blocks; in the mouths of the loving it stays, sunk deep and settled.
1174.nuance: A Vaishnava name in a Saiva Siddhar's mouth, which fits the poet's refusal of 'your god and ours' in 1186. ஒன்பதாம் may make the name the ninth, or pair the nine-lettered name with the nine gates. நோய் அடைப்பதாம் is uncertain: the name becomes a blockage in the spiteful, or blocks disease. The stanza's plain claim is that the mouth that says the name, not the name, decides its effect.

1175.reading: What is the water you scoop up and pour? What is the thing you knead in your palm? You fools who mumble under your breath: what is this guise of deceit, this shutting of the eyes? Gently now, gurus, tell us, tell us.
1175.nuance: The rite is the water-offering with the kneaded rice or clay ball (பிண்டம்) and muttered mantra; the shut eyes are the show of meditation. The last line turns on the addressed 'fools' being 'gurus', said with மெள்ளவே (softly) twice, which is mock courtesy.

1176.reading: The seed set in the impurity of the mother's womb, having been carried before, becomes a drop like dew; the inner heat too subsides within that impurity; and what is born afterwards is itself impurity, you madmen.
1176.nuance: Line 3 (உன்னிதொக் குளழலும்) is garbled; 'the heat within' is a guess from உள் அழல். முன்னையே தரித்தும், carried before, may mean the seed was first borne in the father, or that the soul bore a former body. The stanza's argument is the body's origin in blood and seed, made to shame pride in it.

1177.reading: You who bathe daily to remove the dirt and whose dirt is never removed: where was the dirt, and where is what is without beauty? If you can cut the dirt in the place where the dirt was, you can live close to the Light that has no dirt.
1177.nuance: அழுக்கு is said seven times. The question 'where was the dirt' is the whole argument: if the dirt is in the mind, water cannot reach it. அழகில்லாதது (what has no beauty) is odd beside அழுக்கு and may be a play on the sound; the Light without dirt is the Lord.

1178.reading: Gathered from atoms into a mass, through every kind of womb, you were born a human and now lose yourselves in recited books. What is birth, what is death; passing through the still forms of life, what is thinking, what is standing? Think it through for yourselves.
1178.nuance: அணுத்திரண்ட (atoms gathered) and பல் யோனி (many wombs) give an account of how a human came to be, from matter and through other births, before the books; தாபரம் (the immovable, plants) is among the forms passed through. The verse does not answer its questions and tells the hearer to (நீர் நினைந்து பாரும்), which is its point against recited books.

1179.reading: For the jnanis who have gained and known within themselves, untaught, the Soma of scripture and sound who stands as light, who is the beginning, beyond the cosmos and beyond that again, there is not the least thing called caste difference; there is none.
1179.nuance: சாதிபேதம் is denied for the knower, not argued away for everyone: the stanza's subject is the jnanis, and the denial is doubled (சற்றும் இல்லை இல்லையே). போதியாமல், without being taught, excludes the guru too. சுருதி நாத சோமன் names the Lord as the moon of Veda and sound, a yogic epithet.

1180.reading: In the first cause the body does not age. Fold the tongue back toward the nose, go up by the channel of sound, and if you can hold the pair pressed hard with longing cut away, then look and look and every direction becomes the supreme Brahman.
1180.nuance: The tongue folded toward the nose is the khechari seal; நாத நாடி, the channel of sound, is the central channel. இரட்டை (the pair) is unexplained, in tradition the in- and out-breaths or the two side channels, and ஏக்கறுத்து may be 'cutting longing' or a form of ஏக்கம் (panting). The first line's claim that the body does not age at the source is the Siddhars' deathlessness, stated as a condition reached by the practice.

1181.reading: Five and five and five and five stand making trouble; five and five and five sit settled within; if you can sustain five and five and five, then five and five sit settled within you: Sivayam.
1181.nuance: A count-cipher in fives: twenty that trouble, fifteen within, fifteen to sustain, ten settled. Tradition sets the twenty as the five elements, five senses, five sense-objects and five organs of action, the fifteen or ten as the breaths and faculties; the division is not fixed. The last line's ten may also be the five letters twice, which the refrain suggests.

1182.reading: What is it that stands settled as the first of the five letters? What is it you chant, standing in the letter of the heart? What is it that the sword of the five letters cuts? You must separate out and tell the straight truth of the unripe letter.
1182.nuance: Three questions on the mantra's inside: its first (ஆதி), its place (நெஞ்சு), its work (அறுப்பு, cutting, as a sword). பிஞ்செழுத்து, the unripe or budding letter, is obscure, perhaps the seed-syllable or the letter before it is sounded; 1142's flower without a bud may be its pair.

1183.reading: Where was the life before it took up the body? What is life, and what is the body? What is it that joins life and body? You true jnani who took up a body by life, tell me.
1183.nuance: The same questions as 1131, now about life (உயிர்) and body alone, with a third added: what joins them. The jnani addressed is one who 'took up a body by life', that is, anyone born, so the question is turned on every hearer who claims knowledge.

1184.reading: Set the one letter that curls at the mouth of speech; the root channels pass beyond pain and pleasure; raise the pressed letter within the fire, mingle the six lotuses, and in the place beyond ...
1184.nuance: The stanza has no main clause and reads as the first half of a longer unit, or as a list of stages with the result lost. சுழித்த ஓர் எழுத்து, the curling letter, is Om in its written form, or the letter உ; ஆறு பங்கயம், the six lotuses, are the six centres; the pressed letter raised in the fire is the seed-syllable at the root. The place beyond (அப்புறத் தலம்) is the crown or what is above it.

1185.reading: Before form was taken, the sound that life entered; before conception, what the body was: blood; before grace is received, understanding is the root support. Mark this and know it, you gurus whose virtue is gone.
1185.nuance: The third set of answers to 1131's questions, and different from 1132's: there the body was in fire and desire in wind, here the body was blood (சோணிதம்) and life entered as sound. அறிவு மூலாதாரம் may mean understanding is the root centre, or is the root support of grace. The gurus addressed are abused in the same breath they are taught.

1186.reading: Once the Lord who is everywhere has entered our body, they still parcel him into shares and will not come near the hard way. 'Our god, your god': are there two? The difference is yours alone; in truth there is no second.
1186.nuance: பங்கு கூறு போடுவார், they divide into shares, is said of the sectarians who split the one Lord; பாடு சென்று அணுகிலார் may mean they will not approach the labour of the path, or will not approach the body where he is. The verse's claim is not that the gods are equal but that there is one, and that the two are made by the speakers.

1187.reading: Being Hari and being Brahma, being one everywhere in the cosmos, being great, the foot that stood in the world: is it not one? You fools in guise who made it other by saying 'it is spread out': look with understanding, and here and there it is one.
1187.nuance: Hari and Brahma are named as the one's forms, so the oneness claimed in 1186 includes the Vaishnava's god. விரிவது என்று, 'saying it spreads', is the sectarian's error: taking the one's extension as many. பாதம் ஒன்று, the one foot, may be the Lord's foot or the one ground.

1188.reading: You smear the burnt ash on your body and take up the guise; the mantra you think of in the mind and repeat each day: is it in the former mantra, in the root mantra, or in which mantra that the Lord comes and moves?
1188.nuance: The question is rhetorical and its force is that the Lord moves in none of them, but the stanza stops at the question. வெந்த நீறு, burnt ash, names the holy ash by its making rather than its holiness. முந்து மந்திரம் and மூல மந்திரம் are the initiatory and root mantras of a tradition; the poet does not say which tradition.

links.note: Tirumanthiram 979 says SIVAYA joined becomes the soul's enjoyment and knowledge, grace settles in the clarified soul, and becoming that Siva is release. 1165 says that clarified (தெளிந்து) in the five letters Sivayam one may become a god, rule the sky and grasp the truth. Both make clarity in the five letters the way, and both rank the truth or the Siva-state above what else the mantra gives.

Both make the body a clay pot. The Naladiyar's pot seeps filth from nine openings and only a fool calls it a woman; Sivavakkiyar's false pot (பொய்க்குடம்) tosses on the water when it holds only the five, and sits content when it has scooped up Siva. The same vessel is a cause for disgust in one and, filled rightly, a seat of delight in the other.

Tirumanthiram 1531 calls the Lord the thief-chief who enters and leaves the hollow hut of the body (கள்ளத் தலைவன்). 1167 ends by telling the hearer to bind tight the thief who knows the theft (களவறிந்த கள்வன்). If Sivavakkiyar's thief is the Lord, the stanza asks for what Tirumular's laments the lack of: holding the one who comes and goes. If it is the mind, the image is the same and the thief different.

Tirumanthiram 2204 ends its states of deep sleep with turiya as a void beyond words (வாக்கிறந்த பாழ்). 1168 describes the truth of the blissful nature where speech has died and mind has died (சொல்லிறந்த மனமிறந்த). Both place the goal past speech and mind; Sivavakkiyar adds that even the inner Brahman dies there, and that night and day, the states themselves, are gone.

Naladiyar 46 lists entrails, fat, blood, bone, sinew, skin and flesh and asks which part is the woman. 1169 lists what ten months of the womb's impurity became, two hands, two feet, two eyes, a body of sound, taste and smell, and says the 'pure' body is that impurity. Both take the body apart to deny it worth; the Naladiyar's aim is desire for a woman, Sivavakkiyar's pride in one's own body and birth.

Tirumanthiram 934 says Nandi is seated by the five letters and within the five letters (அஞ்செழுத்துள்ளே அமர்ந்திருந்தானே), making mantra, diagram and Lord one. 1171 says the thing itself is not the five letters nor the three (அஞ்செழுத்தும் மூன்றெழுத்தும் அல்ல காணும் அப்பொருள்). The conflict holds if 934's 'within' means identity, as its circling of the word suggests; it dissolves if 934 means only that the Lord dwells in the mantra, which 1171 also allows by pressing the five into the heart.

Both stanzas look behind the five letters. 1171 says the thing is not the five nor the three, and that knowing 'that letter' colours the five; 1182 asks what stands as the first of the five, what the heart's letter is, and what the sword of the five letters cuts. One answers with a hidden letter, the other leaves the questions open, but both refuse to let the mantra be the end.

Tirumanthiram 2987 says that reciting the Lord's thousand names holds one within a thousand protections. 1174 says the name Rama in the mouth of the spiteful comes as disease and blockage, and only in the mouth of the loving stays settled. Sivavakkiyar makes the effect of the name depend on the heart that says it; Tirumular's promise has no such condition.

Both open with the water rite: 1129 'you scoop water and pour it into water', 1175 'what is the water you scooped and poured?'. 1129 goes on to offer thought on the root and seed as what reaches Siva; 1175 only widens the mockery to the kneaded ball, the muttering, the guise and the shut eyes, and calls the performers gurus. The second stanza is the first without its positive half.

Kural 274 likens the man who hides in austerity and does what is not austerity to a hunter in a bush snaring birds. 1175 asks what the false guise (கள்ள வேடம்) and the shut eyes are for, and calls the mumblers fools and then gurus. Both treat religious show as a hunter's cover; the Kural says what the hunter takes, Sivavakkiyar only exposes the bush.

Thiruppugazh 520 traces the poet's life from a drop like dew in the womb (பனித்துளி), growing to a doll of nine gates. 1176 says the seed set in the mother's womb becomes a drop like dew (பனித்துளி போலாகுமே) and what is born of it is impurity. The same dewdrop opens both accounts of the body; Arunagiri's ends in a plea for the feet, Sivavakkiyar's in a rebuke to the proud.

Kural 278 says many bathe as though distinguished and go about concealed, with impurity in their minds (மனத்தது மாசாக). 1177 addresses those who bathe daily to remove dirt whose dirt is never removed, and asks where the dirt was. Both say water misses the dirt that matters; the Kural reports it of hypocrites, Sivavakkiyar tells the bathers where to cut.

Kural 298 divides purity: outer purity comes by water, inner purity is seen through truth. 1177 says daily bathing leaves the dirt and asks where the dirt was, so that it can be cut there. Sivavakkiyar's 'where' is the Kural's 'inner'; the Kural grants water its outer purity, Sivavakkiyar grants it nothing.

Kural 357 says that if the mind ponders and knows with certainty what is, one need not think again of birth. 1178 tells those lost in recited books to ask for themselves what birth, death, thought and standing are (நீர் நினைந்து பாருமே). Both put the mind's own inquiry above learning as the way past birth; Sivavakkiyar names the books as the obstacle.

Tirumanthiram 2957 says that for those who set Nandi firmly in love by knowledge there is no impurity, no pride and no caste (குலமில்லை). 1179 says that for the jnanis who have known the Lord within themselves there is not the least thing called caste difference (சாதிபேதம்). Both deny caste for the knower rather than for everyone; Tirumular's knower reaches by love, Sivavakkiyar's untaught (போதியாமல்).

Naladiyar 195 says 'good caste' and 'bad caste' are words with nothing behind them, and that austerity, learning and effort make a lineage. 1179 says caste difference does not exist at all for those who have known the Lord within. Both empty the word of substance; the Naladiyar replaces birth with merit, Sivavakkiyar with knowledge, and only Sivavakkiyar says there is nothing there (இல்லையே).

Tirumanthiram 1658 ranks the wearers of the garb by line: men of low birth put it on to rise, men of the right line to become gods, and the outcast ones are to be weeded out. 1179 says there is not the least caste difference for the knower. The conflict holds if 1658's குலம் words mean birth-caste, as its first line (இழிகுலத்தோர்) suggests; if they are words for conduct, as its own marking allows, the two need not clash.

Tirumanthiram 809 says to raise the tongue by the way of the body's water, drink the honey-water and say Sivaya nama. 1180 says to fold the tongue back toward the nose (நாக்கை மூக்கையுள் மடித்து), go by the channel of sound and hold the pair pressed. Both give the khechari seal, the tongue turned back, as the practice; Tirumular ends in nectar and the mantra, Sivavakkiyar in every direction becoming Brahman.

Tirumanthiram 647 says that in the eighth stage of practice grey hair and wrinkles do not appear. 1180 opens with the claim that in the first cause the body does not age (ஆக்கை மூப்பது இல்லையே), and gives the tongue and channel practice that reaches it. Both make the body's ageing stop as a result of yoga; Sivavakkiyar locates the agelessness in the source rather than in a counted year.

Tirumanthiram 977 says five elephants live in the forest, the five letters are their goad, and for those who hold all five together the First beyond the five can enter within. 1181 counts fives that make trouble and fives that sit within, and says that for those who can sustain the fives, the fives sit settled within as Sivayam. Both make mastery of the fives the condition for the Lord's settling within; Sivavakkiyar multiplies the count to twenty.

Kural 340 asks whether the life that lodges in the body has no home of its own. 1183 asks where life was before it took up the body, what joins life and body, and tells the jnani who took a body to answer. Both treat the body as the soul's lodging and ask after the soul's own place; the Kural's question is about impermanence, Sivavakkiyar's about origin.

Thiruppugazh 1313 traces an ascent from the four-petalled lotus through the centres to bindu, nada and the sound beyond, and asks to be sent out by the root gate into the light. 1184 sets the curling letter at the mouth, raises the pressed letter in the fire, mingles the six lotuses (ஆறு பங்கயம்) and reaches the place beyond. Both are compressed itineraries of the yoga of the centres; Arunagiri's is a plea, Sivavakkiyar's an instruction without its last clause.

Both answer 1131's questions about what was before form, conception and grace. 1132 says the body was in fire and desire in the wind; 1185 says life entered as sound, the body was blood, and understanding is the root support before grace. The two answer sets do not match, which shows that the refrain, not the physiology, is what the poet holds fixed.

Tirumanthiram 1087 says the many gods appear different as ornaments appear many though they are one gold, and the Mistress is the cause of Siva, Brahma and Vishnu. 1186 says 'our god, your god' are not two, and that the difference is the speakers' own. Both make the plurality of gods a seeming; Tirumular explains it by one material in many forms, Sivavakkiyar by human partition (பங்கு கூறு).

Thiruppugazh 257 asks why the deceitful siddhas and those confused by the six sects consecrate many gods, fix names and set up images, dividing themselves only to be reborn. 1186 says those who parcel the one Lord into 'our god, your god' make a difference that is theirs alone. Both charge the sects with manufacturing plurality; Arunagiri includes the siddhas among the dividers, which is a charge Sivavakkiyar would turn back on the sects.

Tirumanthiram 311 says the able live joined to the one way while others say knowledge is many, and that the unlearned do not know God mingled in all. 1187 says the one that is Hari and Brahma and fills the cosmos is one foot, and that those in guise who say 'it is spread out' and make it many should look with understanding and see it one here and there. Both make plurality the error of the unknowing and pervasion the mark of the one.

Tirumanthiram 1666 says that for those who wear the holy ash gladly and never let it fade, deeds will not stay and the Siva state will come. 1188 addresses those who smear burnt ash and take up the guise and asks in which of their mantras the Lord comes and moves, implying none. The conflict holds if 1188's question is a denial, as the stanza's tone suggests; if it only asks for the right mantra, it leaves the ash untouched.

1174 says the name works in the mouth of the loving and turns to disease in the mouth of the spiteful. 1188 asks in which daily mantra, former or root, the Lord moves. Read together, 1174 supplies the answer 1188 withholds: not in any mantra as such, but in the heart that says it.

new_concepts.gloss: the beginningless: what has no origin, asked by the Siddhars of the letter, the soul, the elements, scripture, the guru and Siva himself, and claimed for the knower
new_concepts.label_source: The verse uses the word: 1173 (அனாதியோ, five times); also declared in ch061 and ch062.

new_concepts.gloss: the womb's impurity: the menstrual blood and seed from which the body is formed, named by the Siddhars to shame pride in body, birth and caste
new_concepts.label_source: The verses use the word: 1159 (தூமையின் முளைத்தெழுந்த சீவன்), 1169 (அடங்கிநின்ற தூமைதான், சொல்லுகின்ற தூமையே), 1176 (அன்னைகர்ப்பத் தூமையில், தூமைகாணும்).

source_issues: 1184 has no main clause and ends mid-sentence (அப்புறத் தலத்துளே); it reads as the first half of a longer unit or a stanza whose last line has been lost.
1168 line 4 சொல்லியாற cannot be construed as it stands (ஆறு, the way, or a corrupt word).
1176 line 3 உன்னிதொக் குளழலும் is garbled; read by guess as 'the heat within'.
1173 line 1 ஆத்துமா for ஆத்துமம் (as in 1126) and 1181's repeated அஞ்சும் with no nouns are as the source has them; 1181 may have lost its glossing words in transmission.
1174 line 2 ராமராம ராம is the only Vaishnava name-mantra in this run; it is not a misattribution, since the stanza's own argument depends on it.
